replies.rawMarkdown:
Please do! If you were to create an ARC-like game from scratch, I'd say have a health bar, a difficulty progression where later levels introduce new mechanics, let the first level be a tutorial level, seed your RNGs, and no cultural symbols (aliens from Zeta Reticuli should be able to play).

But any ARCEngine games are welcome.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
In short, ARC3.Games is an open source, browser-based ARCEngine game player connected to an open database that stores gameplay.

Why? Initially as part of porting [PushWorld](https://deepmind-pushworld.github.io/play/) to the ARCEngine, to have a more user-friendly way to interact with games. There is the game player on the ARCPrize website, but it is baked into the site, and not open source, so you can't play your custom games with it. The [ARC-AGI Tookit](https://docs.arcprize.org/toolkit/overview) is just for letting computers play the games, with primitive rendering capabilities, and nothing much for humans.

Another reason for ARC3.Games is to crowdsource gameplay data to be used for creating capable AI agents. Each time a player finishes a level, their performed action sequence gets sent to the server, verified, and put into the open database, accessible through the API. Only action sequences that finish a level get recorded; game overs do not. Resets do not get recorded either. When a player resets a game, the action sequence for that level gets cleared.

Unlike the ARCPrize game player, ARC3.Games loads the games locally instead of playing them on a remote server through an API. This is done through a virtual Python environment in the browser, enabled by [PyScript](https://pyscript.net/).

There are 30 games in the library: 25 public games, 4 public preview games, and the PushWorld port ("pw14-c1586e55"), which is a partial port — just the games that would fit within the 64x64 frame.

Check it out:
https://arc3.games/
